body:
Routed from the getwyrd/wyrd-pdca Act review of 2026-08-02. The instance fix is applied there (`engine/scripts/run-verify.sh`); filing here because the script is **template-rendered**, so the same false-PASS exists in every instance that renders it.

## The defect

`run-verify.sh`'s RED leg reverts the production change, keeps the added test, and expects a failing assertion. It decided the verdict from cargo's exit status alone:

```sh
if run_test; then
  if [ "$TESTS_RAN" -eq 0 ]; then ... exit 77; fi     # the #114 guard — cargo SUCCEEDED branch only
  echo "FAIL — the test PASSES without the fix"; exit 1
fi
echo "run-verify.sh: PASS — red without the fix, green with it."   # <- unconditional
exit 0
```

A **compile error exits non-zero exactly as a failing assertion does**. So when the RED leg fails to build, control skips the zero-test guard (which sits only on the cargo-exited-0 branch) and falls through to the unconditional `PASS`. A bundle whose discriminator never built is recorded as proof that its test catches the bug.

The four cells the leg actually has:

| cargo rc | tests ran | old verdict | correct verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0 | UNVERIFIABLE | UNVERIFIABLE (#114) |
| 0 | >0 | FAIL | FAIL |
| ≠0 | >0 | PASS | PASS |
| **≠0** | **0** | **PASS** | **UNVERIFIABLE** |

## Why it is reachable, not theoretical

A discriminator that calls production API the patch **adds** cannot compile once that production change is reverted — and the RED leg reverts *every* patch-touched production file, keeping only added tests. That is a routine slice shape; the existing `GREEN_ONLY` escape covers only a net-new **crate**, not a net-new symbol in an existing one.

It was already being mitigated in prose: all three briefs in the wyrd instance's 2026-07-25 multipart batch carried a paragraph telling the builder to out-think it (only base-visible symbols; no patch-added crate in a test; record the executed-test count from the RED leg), and two of the three had a concrete instance found only by cross-vendor plan review. Mitigating a gate defect per-brief scales with the number of briefs and depends on a model getting it right every time.

## Why it is the worst direction to fail in

An evidence gate that fails toward *accept* does not lose data — it loses the proof that data is not being lost. `TESTS_RAN` is already computed on both paths (`run_test` parses the captured output and returns cargo's status), so the guard costs nothing to add.

## The instance fix, for reference

getwyrd/wyrd-pdca applied it as a pure helper plus a test hook, so all four cells are unit-pinned without a worktree or cargo:

```sh
_red_verdict() { # <cargo-exit-status> <tests-ran> -> PASS | FAIL | UNVERIFIABLE
  local rc="$1" ran="$2"
  [ "$ran" -eq 0 ] && { printf 'UNVERIFIABLE'; return 0; }
  [ "$rc" -eq 0 ] && { printf 'FAIL'; return 0; }
  printf 'PASS'
}
```

The RED leg routes through it and keeps two distinct UNVERIFIABLE messages (rc 0 = "compiled to nothing"; rc ≠ 0 = "did not build against the reverted base — the usual cause is a test calling production API this patch adds"), both exit 77 → §6 NEEDS-HUMAN, never a patch verdict. Six new cases in `engine/tests/test_run_verify.sh` pin the matrix, including that any non-zero status behaves identically (101 / 1 / 134) because what decides the verdict is whether a test executed, not which code cargo returned.

## Expected cost

Slices whose RED leg genuinely cannot compile now raise a §6 item instead of passing silently. That is the honest reading, and it is visible rather than free: the human either splits the test so it exercises the behaviour through pre-existing API, or records at sign-off why the slice has no isolable red.

## Origin

getwyrd/wyrd-pdca#178 queued this as PROPOSED on 2026-07-26 ("the script is harness-rendered, so the fix is upstream template feedback rather than an instance edit"); applied and filed at the 2026-08-02 Act pass (`process/act-log.md`).
title: run-verify: the RED leg scores a compile failure as PASS — the evidence gate fails toward accept
